# How Biscuit

> Practical, evidence-aware guides for technology, home, kitchens, shopping decisions, and useful tools.

How Biscuit is an independent practical-guides publication operated by Boho Digital Services.
This build has no affiliate links, sponsored placements, paid reviews, or product placements.

## Public pages

- [2.4 GHz vs. 5 GHz Wi-Fi: Which Should You Use?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/2-4-ghz-vs-5-ghz-wifi/): Use 2.4 GHz when range and wall penetration matter; use 5 GHz when a nearby device needs more capacity. Learn why the router may choose automatically.
- [Air-Drying vs. Clothes Dryer: Cost, Time, and Fabric Tradeoffs](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/air-drying-vs-clothes-dryer/): Air drying reduces dryer energy and can reduce fabric wear, but requires time, space, ventilation, and humidity control. Compare cost, weather, pollen, and fabric needs.
- [Air Fryer vs. Oven Electricity Cost](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/air-fryer-vs-oven-electricity-cost/): Compare exact wattage, preheat, cooking time, batches, and servings. A small air fryer often uses less for a small meal, but capacity can reverse the result.
- [Air Purifier vs. HVAC Filter: Which Do You Need?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/air-purifier-vs-hvac-filter/): Portable air cleaners treat one room or area. HVAC filters work throughout a ducted system only while its fan runs. Learn when one, both, or neither solves the problem.
- [Apartment Move-In Inspection Checklist: Document Damage Before You Unpack](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/apartment-move-in-inspection-checklist/): Inspect every room before moving furniture inside. Photograph existing damage, test essential systems, and submit the condition report on time.
- [Appliance Buying Checklist: Measurements, Hookups, Delivery, Warranty, and Recalls](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/appliance-buying-checklist/): Measure the space and delivery route, verify every hookup, read EnergyGuide and warranty terms, inspect delivery damage, check recalls, and document installation.
- [Are Extended Warranties on Appliances Worth It?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/appliance-extended-warranty-worth-it/): Compare the service contract with the manufacturer warranty, repair risk, deductibles, exclusions, shipping, reimbursement limits, claims process, and provider reputation.
- [Best Place to Put Your Wi-Fi Router](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/best-place-to-put-wifi-router/): Put your router near the center of the area you use, out in the open, off the floor, and away from dense barriers. Use this test before buying an extender.
- [Can a 100-Watt USB-C Charger Damage Your Phone?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-100w-usb-c-charger-damage-phone/): A 100-watt USB-C laptop charger can usually charge a compatible phone safely. Learn how power negotiation works and which warning signs matter.
- [Can a Microwave Interfere With Wi-Fi?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-microwave-interfere-with-wifi/): A microwave oven can interfere with nearby 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi while it is running. Test the pattern, move equipment, or use 5 GHz or 6 GHz where supported.
- [Can You Freeze Eggs?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-freeze-eggs/): How to freeze raw egg whites or whole eggs safely without putting shell eggs in the freezer.
- [Can You Freeze Milk?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-freeze-milk/): You can freeze pasteurized milk in a freezer-safe container with expansion space, then thaw it in the refrigerator. Texture may separate, so shake or blend it after thawing.
- [Can You Mix Bleach and Vinegar?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-mix-bleach-and-vinegar/): Never mix chlorine bleach and vinegar. The combination can release toxic chlorine gas. Leave the area for fresh air and contact emergency or poison help if exposure occurs.
- [Can You Paint Over Mold?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-paint-over-mold/): Paint can hide mold temporarily, but it does not remove the growth or fix the moisture that caused it. Clean, dry, and repair the area first.
- [Can You Plug an Air Conditioner Into an Extension Cord?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-plug-air-conditioner-into-extension-cord/): A room air conditioner should normally plug directly into a grounded wall outlet, not an extension cord. Here is the safe response when its factory cord will not reach.
- [Can You Plug a Space Heater Into a Power Strip?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-plug-space-heater-into-power-strip/): Space heaters should be plugged directly into a wall outlet, not into a power strip or extension cord. Here is why and what to do when the cord will not reach.
- [Can You Put Dish Soap in a Dishwasher?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-put-dish-soap-in-dishwasher/): Why ordinary hand-washing liquid does not belong in an automatic dishwasher and what to do after an accidental dose.
- [Can You Put Hot Food Directly in the Refrigerator?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-put-hot-food-in-refrigerator/): Hot food can go directly into the refrigerator, but large batches should be divided into shallow containers so they cool quickly and safely.
- [Can You Refreeze Food After a Power Outage?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-refreeze-food-after-power-outage/): You can refreeze food that still contains ice crystals or remains at 40°F or below. Discard perishables held above 40°F for more than two hours.
- [Can You Use Soap on Cast Iron?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/can-you-use-soap-on-cast-iron/): Yes. A small amount of mild dish soap is generally safe for seasoned cast iron. Wash by hand, dry promptly, and apply a very thin coat of oil if needed.
- [How to Check for Recalls Before Buying a Used Product](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/check-recalls-before-buying-used-product/): A used product can look perfect and still be recalled. Search the exact model, serial number, production date, or VIN before paying.
- [Why Are Clothes Taking So Long to Dry?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/clothes-taking-too-long-to-dry/): Long drying time often starts with airflow, lint, venting, load size, washer spin, sensors, cycle choice, room temperature, or a heating fault. Check safety before running another cycle.
- [Cold vs. Warm vs. Hot Water for Laundry](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/cold-vs-warm-vs-hot-water-laundry/): Cold water saves the most energy and works for many ordinary loads. Warm or hot water may be needed for oily soil, care-label instructions, sanitation, or exact detergent and washer requirements.
- [Why Is My Dehumidifier Running but Not Collecting Water?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/dehumidifier-running-not-collecting-water/): A dehumidifier may stop collecting because the room is already below the setpoint, the room is too cold, airflow is blocked, the bucket or drain is wrong, or the compressor has failed.
- [Dehumidifier vs. Air Conditioner: Which Do You Need?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/dehumidifier-vs-air-conditioner/): An air conditioner removes heat and some moisture. A dehumidifier removes moisture but returns heat to the room. Choose from temperature, humidity, moisture source, and room conditions.
- [Do Ceiling Fans Cool a Room? What They Actually Do](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/do-ceiling-fans-cool-a-room/): Ceiling fans make people feel cooler by moving air, but they do not meaningfully lower an empty room’s temperature. Here is when to run one, when to turn it off, and how to pair it with air conditioning.
- [Do You Have to Preheat the Oven?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/do-you-have-to-preheat-oven/): Preheat for most baking and whenever a recipe or package says to. Some roasts and casseroles can start in a cold oven, but food-safety temperatures still govern doneness.
- [Do You Need a Refrigerator Thermometer? What to Look For](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/do-you-need-refrigerator-freezer-thermometer/): Keep one appliance thermometer in the refrigerator and one in the freezer. Learn what type to buy, where to place it, and how to read it.
- [Does Aluminum Foil Improve Wi-Fi Signal?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/does-aluminum-foil-improve-wifi-signal/): Metal can redirect Wi-Fi, but the famous study used computer-optimized 3D reflectors coated with foil. Random kitchen foil can help one direction and hurt another.
- [Does a Dishwasher Use Less Water Than Hand-Washing?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/does-dishwasher-use-less-water-than-hand-washing/): A modern dishwasher, especially an ENERGY STAR certified model run with full loads, usually uses less water than washing the same dishes by hand under a running faucet.
- [Does Turning the AC Off Save Money?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/does-turning-ac-off-save-money/): Turning off or raising the AC when no one is home usually saves energy, but heat, humidity, pets, and health needs determine whether “off” is sensible.
- [Does Unplugging Appliances Save Electricity?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/does-unplugging-appliances-save-electricity/): How standby power works, which devices are practical to switch off, and why measurement beats a universal savings claim.
- [Download Speed vs. Upload Speed vs. Latency](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/download-vs-upload-speed-latency/): Download speed moves data to you, upload moves it away, and latency measures delay. Learn which metric affects streaming, calls, backups, gaming, and remote work.
- [ENERGY STAR vs. EnergyGuide](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/energy-star-vs-energyguide/): EnergyGuide reports standardized energy use and comparison information. ENERGY STAR is a voluntary efficiency certification for eligible products meeting current criteria.
- [Ethernet vs. Wi-Fi: Which Is Faster and More Reliable?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/ethernet-vs-wifi/): Ethernet is usually more consistent and avoids wireless interference, but its real speed is limited by the slowest port, adapter, cable, switch, router, or internet connection.
- [Fan vs. Air Conditioner Cost: How Much Cheaper Is a Fan?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/fan-vs-air-conditioner-cost/): A fan usually costs far less to run than an air conditioner, but it does not lower room temperature. Compare hourly costs and learn when to use each.
- [How to Find and Stop Drafts Around Windows and Doors](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/find-stop-drafts-windows-doors/): Locate the exact moving joint or fixed crack before sealing it. Use weatherstripping on operable edges and caulk on stationary gaps.
- [How to Fix Wi-Fi Dead Zones Without Buying Anything](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/fix-wifi-dead-zones-without-buying-anything/): Map the weak area, move and raise the router, try another band, reduce interference, and test one change at a time before buying mesh or an extender.
- [Why Does My Front-Load Washer Smell?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/front-load-washer-smells/): Musty odor often comes from moisture and detergent residue in the gasket, dispenser, drum, filter, or drain area. Clean the exact model correctly and prevent moisture from remaining.
- [Heat Pump vs. Standard Electric Water Heater](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/heat-pump-vs-electric-water-heater/): Heat-pump water heaters move heat from surrounding air and may use resistance backup. Compare efficiency, recovery, room size, temperature, noise, condensate, and installation.
- [Home Energy Check for a High Summer Electric Bill](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/home-energy-check-high-summer-bill/): Use this step-by-step home energy checklist to find why a summer electric bill increased, from billing days and rates to AC filters, air leaks, and hidden loads.
- [Home Humidity and Dehumidifier Checklist](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/home-humidity-dehumidifier-checklist/): Measure humidity room by room, find moisture sources, choose dehumidifier capacity, check drainage and safety, and download the printable three-day room log.
- [Home Wi-Fi Dead-Zone Checklist](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/home-wifi-dead-zone-checklist/): Record Wi-Fi performance room by room, test one change at a time, and decide whether the problem is your device, router placement, or internet service.
- [How Does Baking Powder Work?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-does-baking-powder-work/): Baking powder makes batter and dough rise by producing carbon dioxide bubbles. Here is what triggers it, what goes wrong, and how to test your can.
- [How Long Can Cooked Food Sit Out?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-long-can-cooked-food-sit-out/): Most perishable cooked food should be refrigerated within two hours, or within one hour when the temperature is above 90°F. Food held safely hot or cold follows different rules.
- [How Long Does Cooked Rice Last in the Fridge?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-long-does-cooked-rice-last/): Refrigerate cooked rice within two hours and use it within four days. Cool it promptly in shallow containers and reheat leftovers to 165°F.
- [How Long Is Food Safe in the Refrigerator Without Power?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-long-food-safe-refrigerator-without-power/): An unopened refrigerator keeps food safe for about four hours during an outage. After that, move perishables to ice at 40°F or below or discard them.
- [How Long Will Food Stay Frozen During a Power Outage?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-long-food-stay-frozen-power-outage/): A full unopened freezer holds a safe temperature for about 48 hours; a half-full freezer for about 24 hours. Check temperature and ice crystals afterward.
- [How Long Do Hard-Boiled Eggs Last in the Fridge?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-long-hard-boiled-eggs-last-fridge/): Refrigerate hard-boiled eggs within two hours and use them within one week. Store them at 40°F or below.
- [How Long Do Leftovers Last in the Fridge?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-long-leftovers-last-fridge/): Most cooked leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in a refrigerator at 40°F or below. Refrigerate within 2 hours, use shallow containers, and reheat leftovers to 165°F.
- [How Much Does an Air Purifier Cost to Run?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-does-air-purifier-cost-to-run/): Calculate air-purifier electricity from watts, runtime, and your local rate, then add replacement-filter cost. Compare CADR, noise, and energy efficiency rather than watts alone.
- [How Much Does a Dehumidifier Cost to Run?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-does-dehumidifier-cost-to-run/): Calculate dehumidifier cost from watts, runtime, measured kWh, or annual certified energy use. A 500-watt full-power example costs about 9 cents per hour at 18.44 cents/kWh.
- [How Much Does a Dishwasher Cost Per Load?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-does-dishwasher-cost-per-load/): Divide annual kWh by annual test cycles, then multiply by your rate. A 240 kWh/year dishwasher works out to about 21 cents per standardized cycle at 18.44 cents/kWh.
- [How Much Does an Electric Dryer Cost Per Load?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-does-electric-dryer-cost-per-load/): Estimate dryer cost from measured or certified kWh per cycle. A standardized electric-dryer example can range from about 17 to 40 cents per test load at 18.44 cents/kWh.
- [How Much Does an Electric Oven Cost Per Hour?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-does-electric-oven-cost-per-hour/): Multiply oven kilowatts by active hours and your electric rate, but account for preheat and thermostat cycling. A 3,000-watt full-power example costs 55 cents per hour at 18.44 cents/kWh.
- [How Much Does a Refrigerator Cost to Run?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-does-refrigerator-cost-to-run/): Multiply the refrigerator's EnergyGuide annual kWh by your local electricity rate. A 400 kWh/year example costs about $6.15 per month at 18.44 cents/kWh.
- [How Much Does a Washing Machine Cost Per Load?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-does-washing-machine-cost-per-load/): Divide the washer's annual EnergyGuide kWh by your actual yearly loads, then multiply by your electric rate. Learn how water temperature and drying change the real cost.
- [How Much Does a Water Heater Cost to Run?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-does-water-heater-cost-to-run/): Use the EnergyGuide annual kWh, therms, or fuel consumption with your local rate. Water-heater cost depends on type, household demand, setpoint, standby loss, and installation.
- [How Much Electricity Does a Microwave Use?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-electricity-does-microwave-use/): Multiply the microwave's electrical input watts by cooking time and your electric rate. A 1,500-watt input example costs about 5 cents for 10 minutes.
- [How Much Internet Speed Do You Need?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-internet-speed-do-you-need/): Add the official bandwidth needs of simultaneous streams and calls, then account for upload, latency, Wi-Fi, and variation. Use this household planning guide.
- [How Much Laundry Detergent Should You Use?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-much-laundry-detergent-use/): Use the detergent label for the exact concentration, washer type, load size, soil, and water hardness. More detergent can leave residue, odor, and poor rinsing.
- [How Often Should You Change Your HVAC Filter?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-often-change-hvac-filter/): There is no universal 30-, 60-, or 90-day rule. Inspect based on filter depth, system runtime, pets, smoke, renovation dust, airflow, and manufacturer guidance.
- [How Often Should You Clean a Dryer Vent?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-often-clean-dryer-vent/): Clean the lint filter every load and clean lint from the vent pipe at least annually. Inspect sooner when drying time, airflow, heat, or lint buildup changes.
- [How Often Should You Replace Your Wi-Fi Router?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-often-should-you-replace-wifi-router/): There is no universal router lifespan. Replace it when support ends, security is obsolete, failures persist, or the hardware cannot meet verified household needs.
- [How Often Should You Test and Replace Smoke Alarms?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/how-often-test-replace-smoke-alarms/): Test smoke alarms at least monthly and replace the whole alarm when it is 10 years old, or sooner if its instructions or failed tests require it.

Verify the seller, exact model, serial, recall status, warranty, return policy, missing parts, damage, sanitation, and installation.

- [Should You Rinse Dishes Before Putting Them in the Dishwasher?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/should-you-rinse-dishes-before-dishwasher/): Usually, no. Scrape off solid food and load the dishwasher without hand-rinsing. Modern machines and detergents are designed to do the washing.

Learn what to disconnect, what to leave alone, and what surge protectors can actually do.

Tankless units heat on demand but remain limited by flow, temperature rise, gas or electrical service, venting, and simultaneous fixtures.
- [Is My Water Heater Leaking? What to Check and When to Shut It Down](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/water-heater-leaking-what-to-do/): Identify visible leaks at connections, drain valves, relief piping, condensate, drain pans, or the tank body. Shut down safely and call qualified service for active or unsafe leaks.

- [What Can an Air Purifier Remove?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/what-can-air-purifier-remove/): Air purifiers can reduce some airborne particles such as smoke, dust, pollen, and pet allergens. They do not repair mold, remove radon, or replace carbon-monoxide alarms.
- [What Food Should You Throw Away After a Power Outage?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/what-food-throw-away-after-power-outage/): Discard refrigerated meat, milk, eggs, soft cheese, leftovers, and other perishables after four hours without safe cooling. Use this item-by-item guide.
- [What Humidity Should Your House Be?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/what-humidity-should-house-be/): Keep indoor relative humidity around 30% to 50% when practical and below 60%. Learn how seasons, condensation, basements, leaks, and measurement affect the right target.
- [What MERV Rating Should You Use in Your House?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/what-merv-rating-should-i-use/): EPA recommends MERV 13, or the highest filter your HVAC fan and filter slot can accommodate. Learn how fit, airflow, smoke, pets, and system limits change the answer.
- [What Size Air Purifier Do You Need?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/what-size-air-purifier-do-i-need/): Size an air purifier by room area, ceiling height, target particle, and Clean Air Delivery Rate. EPA's estimate starts around 65 cfm per 100 square feet at an 8-foot ceiling.
- [What Size Dehumidifier Do You Need?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/what-size-dehumidifier-do-i-need/): Choose dehumidifier capacity from the space size and how damp it is. ENERGY STAR recommends 20-30 pints for many damp rooms under 2,000 square feet and more for wetter or larger spaces.
- [What Temperature Should a Freezer Be?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/what-temperature-should-freezer-be/): The safe freezer target, how to measure it, and what to check when the compartment runs warmer than expected.
- [What Temperature Should a Refrigerator Be?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/what-temperature-should-refrigerator-be/): Keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below and the freezer at 0°F. Verify the actual temperature with an appliance thermometer and allow air to circulate.
- [Where Should You Place a Wi-Fi Extender?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/where-to-place-wifi-extender/): Put the extender roughly halfway between the router and weak area, but only where it still receives a strong upstream signal. Test the link before moving farther.
- [Why Are Some Answers Better Than Others?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-are-some-answers-better-than-others/): A useful answer addresses the real question, explains its reasoning, shows the next move, and makes the limits of its evidence visible.
- [Why Does Bluetooth Keep Disconnecting?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-bluetooth-keeps-disconnecting/): Repeated Bluetooth drops usually come from low accessory power, distance, competing paired devices, stale pairing data, power-saving settings, software problems, or failing hardware.
- [Why Bread Goes Stale Faster in the Refrigerator](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-bread-goes-stale-in-refrigerator/): Refrigeration can slow mold, but ordinary refrigerator temperatures accelerate the starch changes that make bread firm and stale.
- [Why Does My Dishwasher Leave a White Film on Dishes?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-dishwasher-leaves-white-film/): White film on dishwasher loads is often mineral residue or detergent film, but permanent glass etching can look similar. Use a simple wipe test, then adjust water, detergent, and rinse aid.
- [Why Do LED Light Bulbs Flicker?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-do-led-light-bulbs-flicker/): LED flicker commonly comes from an incompatible dimmer, a non-dimmable bulb, a poor driver, a loose connection, or unstable power. Here is how to narrow it down safely.
- [Why Do Windows Condense in Winter?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-do-windows-condense-in-winter/): Winter window condensation forms when humid indoor air meets glass cold enough to fall below the air’s dew point. Here is how to reduce it and when it signals a larger moisture problem.
- [Why Does My GFCI Outlet Keep Tripping?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-does-gfci-outlet-keep-tripping/): A GFCI that keeps tripping may be detecting leakage current, moisture, a faulty appliance, or a wiring problem. Use this safe isolation sequence before calling an electrician.
- [Why Does My Wi-Fi Keep Disconnecting?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-does-my-wifi-keep-disconnecting/): Repeated Wi-Fi drops can come from weak signal, one problem device, modem trouble, power saving, saved settings, or router faults. Diagnose them in this order.
- [Why Is My Electric Bill So High in Summer?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-electric-bill-high-summer/): A high summer electric bill usually comes from more cooling hours, higher rates, a longer billing period, air leaks, or an inefficient system. Here is how to identify the cause.
- [Why Does My Faucet Keep Dripping?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-faucet-keeps-dripping/): A drip from the spout usually means an internal seal, washer, cartridge, valve seat, or ceramic component is no longer sealing.
- [Why Is My Freezer Frosting Up?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-freezer-frosting-up/): Excess frost usually means moist air is entering or the freezer is not defrosting correctly. Check the door, gasket, alignment, food, vents, drain, and model-specific defrost system.
- [Why Does My Hot Water Run Out So Fast?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-hot-water-runs-out-fast/): Hot water may run out because demand increased, the tank is undersized, recovery is slow, an electric element failed, sediment accumulated, or a mixing or dip-tube problem exists.
- [Why Is My Dishwasher Not Drying Dishes?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-is-my-dishwasher-not-drying-dishes/): A model-aware checklist for wet dishes, including cycle settings, rinse aid, loading, plastics, and signs that service may be needed.
- [Why Is My Refrigerator Sweating?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-is-my-refrigerator-sweating/): How humidity, door openings, gasket gaps, blocked vents, and temperature problems can cause moisture inside or outside a refrigerator.
- [Why Is My Smoke Alarm Chirping?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-is-my-smoke-alarm-chirping/): How to distinguish an emergency alarm from a maintenance chirp and check the battery, age, and model-specific signal pattern.
- [Why Is My Wi-Fi So Slow? 12 Things to Check Before Buying Anything](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-is-my-wifi-so-slow/): Slow Wi-Fi can come from weak signal, ISP trouble, congestion, router placement, or one problem device. Use this step-by-step diagnosis before buying new hardware.
- [Why Is My Washing Machine Shaking or Walking?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-is-washing-machine-shaking/): A washer often shakes because the load is unbalanced, the machine is not level, or shipping hardware remains installed. Stop it and check in a safe order.
- [Why Is My Microwave Sparking?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-microwave-is-sparking/): Stop the microwave immediately. Common causes include metal, foil, metallic trim, burned food residue, an incorrectly positioned rack, empty operation, or cavity damage.
- [Why Does My Phone Get Hot While Charging?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-phone-gets-hot-while-charging/): Some warmth is normal during charging, especially with fast charging. Persistent excessive heat, swelling, odors, or a hot connector require attention.
- [Why Is My Refrigerator Leaking Water?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-refrigerator-leaking-water/): Trace water from the first wet point. Common sources include supply lines, filters, ice makers, defrost drains, drain pans, condensation, door seals, or nearby plumbing.
- [Why Salt Melts Ice (and When It Stops Working)](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-salt-melts-ice/): A plain-English field guide to freezing-point depression, brine, the limits of rock salt, and the least-wasteful way to de-ice a walk.
- [Why Does My Toilet Keep Running?](https://howbiscuit.com/articles/why-toilet-keeps-running/): A running toilet usually means water is leaking past the flapper or the fill system is sending water into the overflow tube. A dye test can identify the path.
